examples.knowledge_point: Identifying the Shift and Stretch Applied to an Exponential Decay Curve
examples.problem:
The graph below shows the curve $y = k\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x}+c.$ Determine the values of $k$ and $c$ and find the equation of the curve.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931416/assets/3bf9fe67940a4257bad36511847e5cdb91974993e3be6d113dbc62dadd782134.png)
examples.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote of the curve $y=k\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x}+c$ is $y=c.$ In the graph above, the horizontal asymptote is $y=-5$, hence $c=-5.$

We can solve for $k$ by finding a point on the graph and substituting for $x$ and $y.$ The labeled point on the graph is $(0,-1),$ so we substitute $x=0$ and $y=-1$ into the function and solve for $k\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}k{(\frac{1}{2})}^{x}+c & =y \\ k{(\frac{1}{2})}^{x}-5 & =y \\ k{(\frac{1}{2})}^{0}-5 & =-1 \\ k-5 & =-1 \\ k & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the curve is $y = 4\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x} - 5.$

feedback.problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=\frac{3}{2}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{x}+1?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We start with plotting the graph of $y={(\frac{1}{3})}^{x}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931416/assets/ca12bd6db97d982fd2a9e73dcd9d5da0248ce1a40e582787c3f73480f338a570.png)

Next, we plot the graph of $y=\frac{3}{2}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{x}.$ To do this, we scale the graph above by a factor of $\frac{3}{2}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(0,\frac{3}{2})$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931416/assets/53d2977f07e132aa0e3c3608e8fef82f2d058fb1a99aa828ae8b317b8de6844a.png)

Finally, we plot the graph of $y=\frac{3}{2}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{x}+1.$ To do this, we shift the above graph $1$ unit up. The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,\frac{3}{2})$ to $(0,\frac{5}{2})$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931416/assets/6adc189f0d16cf60044553c13d79297c04f4fbfb2806a9bde6971b203822f17a.png)
